_note:
AUTHORED 2026-09-04 for bodies-v3, the enchantment-CREATURE list. `model_combat` is ON for the first time on this deck: until now the goldfish reported `output.available: false` — "no magnitude series ... that is an absent measurement, not a zero" — so there was no clock to read and no way to ask whether the deck kills anything.

READ THE CLOCK AS A CLOCK. The goldfish has NO BLOCKERS and no opponents, so kill_by_N is measured against one 40-life opponent who never interacts. It OVERSTATES a creature plan by construction — this repo has paid for that once already, when the model preferred a go-wide Edgar refactor that Forge then scored 31/400 against the champion's 50/400 because 1/1 tokens do not connect. It is used here anyway because Forge's AI cannot pilot Zur's attack-to-tutor line at all (measured: Zur attacked in 17-47% of games where a human attacks every turn, since the trigger fires on ATTACK and not on connect), so the alternative is no instrument rather than a better one. The error is in a KNOWN DIRECTION and is identical for every list being compared.

COMMANDER DAMAGE IS GONE as a route, on measurement: 0 of 39 games reached 21, 0.35 commander damage a game, and 2.33 total combat damage against edgar-vampires' 32.30 on the same table. The kill is now a BOARD — Zur's trigger puts an enchantment onto the battlefield, so fetching an enchantment CREATURE is a free body every attack.

ZUR'S TRIGGER IS NOW MODELLED, imperfectly and on purpose — `model_commander_attack_tutor` pulls the highest-mana-value enchantment at MV<=3 from the library onto the battlefield once a turn from the turn after Zur lands. It is a CEILING, not an estimate: a goldfish has no blockers so the commander always attacks, where Forge's AI attacked in 17-47% of games and a real pilot attacks when it is safe. Before this the floor was ZERO — the deck's entire engine was invisible and every figure counted only cards it DREW, which is a systematic understatement of exactly this deck's plan. A ceiling and a floor bound it; one number alone did not. And read the engine figure as a DESCRIPTION, never as evidence of a lift — the same hand writes this file and reads the number, which is why `deck_branch.MEMBERSHIP_AXES` refuses these axes as branch objectives.

targets.label: RESOURCE ENGINE drawn — a draw engine that keeps drawing
targets._why: The deck out-resources the table and then converts; without a repeating engine it is a pile of answers with nothing to answer toward. One-shot selection (Brainstorm, Preordain) is deliberately EXCLUDED — it smooths a hand, it does not refill one.

any_of: Tribute to Horobi // Echo of Death's Wail

targets.label: AN ANSWER drawn — spot removal, a sweeper or a counterspell
targets._why: The table plays at a turn-four clock and some seats hold hard lockout effects. A Zur deck that draws no interaction loses before its commander has attacked twice. Widened 2026-09-03: the engine block named this the bottleneck at 0.709 by turn three, and the fix is COUNT, not cost — eight of the original ten were already MV<=2.

targets.label: KILL — a BOARD: a real body plus a way through
KILL — drain: a payoff plus something to feed it
targets._why: Rebuilt around Vito, which is the CONVERTER the deck was missing: lifegain becomes life loss at full value, so Daybreak Coronet's lifelink turns a connection into twice its damage. Marauding Blight-Priest hits every opponent for 1 on the same trigger, and the constellation pair turn each enchantment that lands into both. NOTE Exquisite Blood and Sanguine Bond are DELIBERATELY ABSENT — either would make this a two-card infinite, which is the thing the pilot rejected. Vito alone is a payoff, not a loop. NOTE ALSO the simulation still cannot see any of it: life loss and death triggers are unmodelled, so this measures the PIECES, never the kill. Underworld Coinsmith sits in the PAYOFF leg only: it is both a payoff and fuel, and leaving it in both let one draw satisfy an AND of ORs twice — the defect `_validate_shared_leg` exists to catch, and it caught it here.

any_of: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose
Tribute to Horobi // Echo of Death's Wail

targets.label: RAMP drawn — an accelerant of any kind
targets._why: Context, not a component: the mana block already reports land drops directly.

targets.label: A TUTOR drawn
targets._why: Context. Tutor density is reported and never scored, and a tutor is only as good as the target it fetches — which is what the routes above are for.
